scope: Reviewed account/profile concepts, username procedure and reference only; not full six-source consolidation.

rows.conflict: Repository redirects, profile/gist URLs and CODEOWNERS have different rename behavior.
rows.requirement: Use stable target identities and inventory all remotes, profile/gist links, mentions and ownership references before approved rename; preview changes, verify current owner and destination, repair references and record post-change behavior including redirect latency. Redirect is not custody.
rows.negative_test: A working old repository redirect cannot pass a rename audit with stale CODEOWNERS or broken gist/profile links; a reclaimed name must not preserve trust.

rows.conflict: Private profile does not hide all fields or create selective-user visibility; cloud warning and pronouns have separate scopes.
rows.requirement: Inventory optional public fields, product/version and intended audience; let the identity owner approve disclosure and verify actual visibility separately from repository access. Do not require personal disclosure as compliance evidence.
rows.negative_test: FPT private profile with public bio or README must not pass a universal nondisclosure claim; GHES cannot inherit cloud-only pronoun availability.

rows.conflict: Unqualified single-account email association conflicts with the managed-user unverified shared-email exception.
rows.requirement: Preserve both claims and independently verify exact account type, enterprise identity provider, email linkage and verification state. Unknown combinations stay unknown; any change requires approved identity-impact plan.
rows.negative_test: Shared unverified EMU email cannot be rejected solely by generic uniqueness prose, nor accepted as verified third-party identity proof.

rows.conflict: Email verification, placeholder API identity, commit attribution and account authentication prove different things.
rows.requirement: Bind observations to stable account identity and current verification/authentication state; record commit-email history separately and check third-party reliance. Attribution or a contribution graph is not authenticated authorship or recovered account custody.
rows.negative_test: Connected commit history or placeholder API email cannot pass authentication/recovery; noreply commits cannot be assumed reconnectable. Numeric-ID noreply attribution retention cannot certify preserved Verified signature status.

rows.conflict: Legacy conversion, modern migration and deletion differ version, preservation and collaboration semantics; legacy collaborator descriptions are ambiguous.
rows.requirement: Require exact platform/authentication/version, explicit target approval, ownership continuity, retained repositories and external participation inventory, plan/diff/apply/verify and proven recovery before lifecycle mutation. Conversion/migration are not interchangeable.
rows.negative_test: GHES >=3.21 cannot inherit legacy conversion; deleting owned content cannot certify deletion of external comments; sole-owner precondition cannot be skipped.

rows.conflict: Single personal identity recommendation coexists with mandatory managed-user separation; protocol choice alone does not prove correct identity.
rows.requirement: Profile actual managed-user requirement and destination visibility; read-only verify repository-scoped identity and remote before approved writes. Keep secrets out of evidence and test wrong-account prevention without granting new credentials.
rows.negative_test: SSH or HTTPS URL alone cannot pass identity separation; a personal account's public capability cannot authorize managed-user public contribution.

rows.conflict: GHES concept introduces built-in only, procedure allows LDAP self-change, and reference requires LDAP administrator change. GHEC managed users cannot self-rename.
rows.requirement: Bind exact platform, version, authentication mode and actor; preserve all source statements and require independent authority verification before proposing rename. An unresolved LDAP matrix remains unknown, not permission or denial inferred from a preferred page.
rows.negative_test: LDAP procedure alone cannot authorize self-rename; reference alone cannot certify every version's behavior; personal-account permission cannot grant managed-user rename.

rows.conflict: Permanent retirement is conditional and pair-specific, while package transfer can still break consumers and other repository redirects can be superseded.
rows.requirement: Before approved rename inventory public Marketplace actions, prior-week clone/Actions-use counts, packages, image visibility/downloads and dependent consumers. Preserve exact >100 and >5,000 thresholds and product scope; unknown telemetry remains unknown. Verify dependency repair and do not assume rollback can recreate a permanently retired name.
rows.negative_test: Exactly 100 uses or 5,000 downloads cannot trigger a strictly greater threshold; private images cannot inherit public-image retirement; namespace transfer cannot prove downstream consumers work or rollback restores retired names.

rows.conflict: New commit-email settings do not rewrite historical commits or transfer educational benefits; cloud push-block/privacy features differ GHES.
rows.requirement: Inventory web and local Git settings plus historical exposure separately; preserve product-specific noreply and push-block capability, and validate approved privacy changes behaviorally. Educational entitlement and old content remain separate.
rows.negative_test: Changing current email cannot mark historical commits scrubbed, GHES cloud privacy supported or educational benefits transferred.

limitations: Negative-test entries are specifications, not implemented or executed tests.
Claim identity validation does not establish semantic equivalence or omission completeness.
No rights clearance, identity mutation, credential change, public publication or native rollout.
